To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present an active visual servoing approach to enable the execution of bimanual grasps on a humanoid robot and we show how the observable workspace is increased by using an additional camera on a humanoid head and how this enables two handed manipulations.

(1) The visual servoing approach enables the robot to execute bimanual grasps and manipulation tasks in real time, (2) the active vision system enables the robot to perceive the environment from different points of view which increases the observable workspace and enables the robot to perform bimanual manipulation tasks, (3) the robot is able to execute manipulation and grasping tasks robustly in real life scenarios.
the proposed framework enables the robot to perform dual arm motions on the basis of visual servoing and that the robot can be used for dual arm grasping as well for dual arm manipulations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the integration of perception and control for the realization of dual arm motions on humanoid robots.
the development of a perception and control framework that enables a humanoid to robustly execute bimanual grasps and manipulations.
the development of a perception system and a control framework for dual arm motions of humanoid robots.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the visual servoing approach presented is able to perform robustly dual arm motions on the humanoid Armar-III.
the proposed approach is able to execute a large variety of tasks with the Armar-III robot in an unstructured environment.
this paper presents a visual servoing based control approach for dual arm motions and manipulations on a humanoid robot that is able to track and grasp objects in a real world scenario.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the humanoid robot is able to execute bimanual tasks in a dynamic environment, where the robot can track the target object(s), the hands as well as the grasped objects and can adapt its motion to the dynamic environment.
the presented approach enables a humanoid robot with two hands to robustly execute bimanual grasps and two handed manipulation tasks in an unstructured environment.
we show how a humanoid robot can be used for executing dual arm tasks with a high level of robustness and reliability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
visual servoing on a humanoid robot can be successfully implemented and is a promising approach to enable robust execution of complex manipulation tasks in unstructured environments.
visual servoing is a viable approach to control the motions of the arms of a humanoid robot in order to achieve a robust grasping and manipulation performance.
a humanoid robot can be used for dual arm tasks in a natural way.
